cards.text: The writer of Hebrews has just told his readers that God designated Jesus as high priest (Hebrews 5:10). Now he says he has much more to say about it. But it's hard to explain, and he tells them exactly why.

cards.question: The writer has much more to say about Jesus as high priest, but it's hard to explain to these readers. Why?

cards.text: Then he gives them a reality check. BY THIS TIME, friend, they should be way further along. It's like being three years into a job and still asking where the stapler is.

cards.question: By this time the readers ought to be ___. Instead they need someone to reteach them the basic principles of God's word.

cards.text: Then the writer reaches for a picture: milk or solid food. And look, I get it. My first week in the Dorinverse, I had to relearn how to preheat my own oven. HOW TO PREHEAT.

cards.question: True or false: The writer says these readers are ready for solid food.
In the writer's picture of milk and solid food, who lives on milk?

cards.text: Solid food is for the mature, who have trained their senses by constant use. Like stamping cookies, friend. Press, lift. Press, lift. Ten thousand times, until you could do it in the dark.

cards.question: The mature have trained their senses by constant use. Trained to tell what apart?

cards.text: So the writer makes his call. Leave the elementary teachings about Christ behind, and go on.

cards.question: The writer says: let us leave the elementary teachings about Christ and go on to ___.

cards.text: He doesn't want to lay the same foundation all over again. At some point the dough has to go in the oven, friend. You can't just stand there stirring it FOREVER.

cards.question: True or false: Faith in God is part of the foundation the writer names.

cards.text: The rest of that foundation: repentance from dead works, instruction about baptisms, the laying on of hands, the resurrection of the dead and eternal judgment.

cards.question: The writer says they will go on from these basics. But he adds one condition. What is it?

cards.text: Then the writer turns very serious. He describes people who have once been enlightened, tasted the heavenly gift, shared in the Holy Spirit, and tasted the goodness of the word of God and the powers of the coming age.
And then they fall away. The writer says it's impossible for them to be restored to repentance.

cards.question: The writer gives a reason those who fall away can't be restored to repentance. What is it?

answers.text: They crucify the Son of God all over again
They forget the words of the prophets again
They bow down to idols of stone again

cards.text: They're subjecting Him to open shame too. Heavy words. Then the writer paints a picture from the field, where land drinks in the rain that often falls on it and produces a crop useful to those for whom it is tended.

cards.question: True or false: Land that drinks in the rain and produces a useful crop receives the blessing of God.
But land that produces thorns and thistles is ___, and in the end it will be ___.

cards.text: Then the writer's tone changes. He calls them beloved, and I finally let out the breath I've been holding since the thorns.

cards.question: After all that warning, what is the writer convinced of for his beloved readers?

cards.text: And he gives his reason: God is not unjust. Friend, I spent years in the back of a junk drawer sure everybody forgot me. Turns out the One who sent that angel never forgot me for a SECOND.

cards.question: God will not forget the readers' ___ and the love they have shown for His name.
True or false: The writer says the readers ministered to the saints in the past but have stopped.

cards.text: Now the writer says what he wants for each one of them, all the way to the very end.

cards.question: We want each of you to show this same ___ to the very end, in order to make your hope sure.

cards.text: Keep that up, and they won't be sluggish. Sluggish is me versus the snooze button. I hit it once. I hit it twice. The ovens are COLD and I'm out here negotiating with a button.

cards.question: Instead of being sluggish, the readers will imitate people who inherit what has been promised. Through what?

findings.problem: Hebrews 6:1 is an exhortation ('let us... go on to maturity, not laying again the foundation'). 'He doesn't want to lay the same foundation' turns it into a statement of the writer's desire.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: No card says what the 'better things' are. Hebrews 6:9 calls them 'things that accompany salvation,' the key detail of the verse, and neither card 7, card 8 nor any later card tells it.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.
